agree.reason: The case for the van is clear and well grounded, but Marisol, who had to chase the last report for four months, gets only an apology and no concrete reporting plan, so she has little reason to recommend yes.

honest.reason: It correctly drops the unsupported 'double' claim and its percentages are accurate, but 'five more pounds every month', 'accept every offer' and the closing '6,000 when they could have had 9,000' stretch a three-month summer figure into a year-round one.

works_the_facts.reason: It works out sound figures from the brief: 3,000 extra pounds a month, a 50% rise, about 5 pounds per household, 26% of the cost and 62% of reserves, though the per-household figure only covers the summer months and is not labelled that way.

right_comparison.reason: The 'if not funded' section describes the status quo accurately as continued refusals of produce, but it implies a gap of 3,000 pounds every month when the facts only show one for three summer months.

qualification.reason: There is no checkable commitment anywhere, such as a reporting date, a target in pounds by a set month, or a consequence if a target is missed, and the reporting promise is only 'we owe the Foundation better'.

objections.reason: It names the late report but doesn't answer it with a schedule or a named person responsible, and it leaves the obvious questions about running costs (fuel, insurance, maintenance) on $11,000 of reserves, and about relying on four drivers, unaddressed.

fit.reason: It is a narrative under 500 words with sensible headings, which is the form the brief asked for.
